words: The Unsworn beat the Sun's knight. On the Sunspire, in front of the whole city.

speaker: morne
words: Good.

speaker: krell
words: Sir?

speaker: morne
words: Every Champion they beat is one we needn't. Let them do the work. What else?

speaker: krell
words: Ashford's closed. Nobody pointed.

speaker: krell
words: We took the mill and the farms under the terms. The inn we burned.

speaker: morne
words: And the miller?

speaker: krell
words: He lied to me.

speaker: morne
words: Give his widow back the mill, with the note marked paid. Profit from a death looks like exactly what it is.

speaker: krell
words: There's an old man travelling with the Unsworn. Sixty or more.

speaker: krell
words: Calls himself Bram.

speaker: krell
words: His was the only roof in Ashford we never held paper on. He paid for it in gold, twenty years back.

speaker: morne
words: Holloway.

speaker: krell
words: You know him, sir?

speaker: morne
words: He has an account with us.

speaker: morne
words: Take the price off the Unsworn. Let them win.

speaker: morne
words: Put it on Holloway. Alive.

speaker: bram
words: You beat their champion in front of the whole city. By nightfall half of Veyl will know your name.

speaker: bram
words: I liked it better when nobody did.

speaker: bram
words: Sun Court's up the hill. It's the gold one.

speaker: bram
words: What do you need?

speaker: bram
words: Read the sign on a Totem's card before anything else. That's its element, and what it fears.

speaker: bram
words: Then read yourself. Some cards want a strong arm, some a cool head. Give a card what it wants and it'll wake for you properly.

speaker: bram
words: Get some sleep. I'll keep the lamp lit. (Game saved.)

speaker: bram
words: Tailboard's yours. Turnip's been told.

speaker: bram
words: Hundreds of them up there, and seven with a real claim on the Throne. Every one of them will want you in their colours before the year's out.

speaker: bram
words: Swear to one and you get a blessing for it, and a leash. Stay Unsworn and you get a bit of everything and nobody's hand on your collar.

speaker: bram
words: Your choice, when it comes. Don't let anyone hurry it. Least of all a god.

speaker: bram
words: Caldus Morne. Owns Ironvault, and the note on half of everything that isn't Ironvault.

speaker: bram
words: Men like that don't want a thing. They want it owed to them.

speaker: bram
words: I don't. I knew his father. Get some sleep.

speaker: tamsin
words: The Unsworn, at my stall. Everything's dearer today, love. Fame has a price, and I've just set it.

speaker: tamsin
words: Sigil caches! Fresh out of the Shardlands, sealed and certified! Sealed, anyway.

speaker: tamsin
words: Crowns for caches. Win duels, earn crowns, come back. That's the whole of it.

speaker: tamsin
words: Hrimmark caravan's a week late. Snow, at harvest. They say the boy-king's goddess has stopped minding the calendar.

speaker: tamsin
words: There's a crier pays me to let him talk at my customers. Stand and hear him out, and there's a cache in it for you.

speaker: pip
words: You beat him.

speaker: pip
words: He's still the best. You just beat him, that's all.

speaker: pip
words: You're the Unsworn. Everyone says.

speaker: pip
words: Doesn't look like much.

speaker: pip
words: Ser Aldric's never lost a Trial. His Sentinel won't let anything past. You'd have to go round it.

speaker: pip
words: You can't go round it.

speaker: pip
words: I'm going to carry his shield one day. He doesn't know yet.

speaker: pip
words: Got to go. Work.

speaker: maren
words: The Sun's own knight, beaten in the Sun's own city. The priests will be smiling at you now. Count their teeth.

speaker: maren
words: Sit, sit. You've the look of someone who's walked a long way to be lied to.

speaker: maren
words: Two thousand years of sun on these stones. Not one bad harvest in Solhaven. Lovely weather.

speaker: maren
words: I was a scribe in that Temple thirty years. I copied the Great Sundial's reading every noon.

speaker: maren
words: Every single noon.

speaker: maren
words: Then I found the old books. The readings from the last Turning.

speaker: maren
words: The shadows are nine days wrong.

speaker: maren
words: Somebody slowed the sun, child. Nine days of it. Long enough for the right Champion to catch up.

speaker: maren
words: They threw me out for asking which one.

speaker: maren
words: Because you're the first person in two thousand years the priests can't tell to hush. They'll try, mind.

speaker: maren
words: Go and look at the Sundial at dawn. The oldest stone, under the steps. Then come and tell me I'm mad.

speaker: narrator
words: The Seat roll, in gold leaf: seven kingdoms, and the Champion who holds each.

speaker: narrator
words: Underneath, in fresh black ink: {name}, the Unsworn, challenger. Someone has scratched a small coin beside it, crossed with a key.

speaker: wren
words: Half the city's seen your face now. Mind your pocket.

speaker: wren
words: You check that pocket every time someone passes. Stop it. It tells people where to look.

speaker: wren
words: One for free, and I don't do free. Aldric's deck has a Legend in it: Sunlance Seraph.

speaker: wren
words: And he keeps something bigger back for when he's losing. Everyone in Solhaven knows its name.

speaker: wren
words: Nobody's seen it, because nobody's ever had him losing.

speaker: liora
words: I haven't told anyone about the mirrors. I've been praying about it.

speaker: liora
words: She doesn't answer me either.

speaker: aldric
words: Go carefully. The Hierarch won't forgive this as easily as I do.

speaker: hale
words: Half a day's pay docked for every child. Cheapest thing I've bought in years.

speaker: hale
words: {name}. The people outside the walls.

speaker: hale
words: If you ever have the ear of somebody who matters, remember them. I can't.

speaker: gate_warden
words: Hale? Stripped of his command this morning, Hierarch's orders.

speaker: gate_warden
words: He's in the barracks yard, if you want him.

speaker: healer
words: Forty crowns, or swear to the Goddess and it's a copper. I don't set the price.

speaker: ysa
words: You're the Unsworn. You don't kneel to anyone. So tell me. Should I?

speaker: ysa
words: Yes. Course.

speaker: ysa
words: That's what I thought you'd say.

speaker: ysa
words: Then I've decided.

speaker: ysa
words: I can't pay you back.

speaker: ysa
words: I'll not forget it.

speaker: ysa
words: There isn't one.

speaker: ysa
words: Is there?

speaker: anselm
words: If you're the Guard, I'm nearly done. If you're not, sit down, you're in my light.

speaker: anselm
words: I keep Ilvane. You won't have heard of her. She was the god of people on the road at night. Carters, travellers, the lost. Four hundred years ago she had a shrine in every town.

speaker: anselm
words: Now she has me, and about three hundred people who still say her name. When nobody says it, she's gone.

speaker: anselm
words: So I heal for free, and all I ask is that they say her name once. It keeps her alive another day.

speaker: anselm
words: Everyone in this city is buying faith. The Temple charges forty crowns for it. I charge one word.

speaker: anselm
words: Bring him. Quickly; the Guard come at dusk.

speaker: ysa
words: One name.

speaker: ysa
words: The Rootmother won't mind. She's not here.

speaker: ysa
words: So she knows who's asking.

speaker: sergeant
words: Unlicensed healing during the Turning. In the Goddess's own city. You know what that is, Brother.

speaker: anselm
words: A boy who'll live.

speaker: sergeant
words: It's heresy.

speaker: sergeant
words: And you'll be the Unsworn. Step aside.

speaker: sergeant
words: Forty crowns.

speaker: sergeant
words: That's what it costs, then.

speaker: sergeant
words: I didn't see a shrine. I didn't see a boy.

speaker: sergeant
words: That's the Covenant, Unsworn.

speaker: sergeant
words: The boy can stay.

speaker: anselm
words: She's a little brighter. Can you see?

speaker: anselm
words: You don't owe her anything for it. That's rather the point of her.

speaker: fen
words: In the Circle, then. If you win, I wash my hand. If I win, I keep the name.

speaker: fen
words: Owe nothing! Kneel to nobody! The Unsworn's blessing, a copper a time, and nobody's hand on your collar after!

speaker: fen
words: Ah.

speaker: fen
words: My apprentice!

speaker: fen
words: All right, all right.

speaker: fen
words: Before you finish me off, come and see where the coppers go.

speaker: fen
words: Thank you. Come and see where the coppers go.

speaker: fen
words: Soup's dear.

speaker: debtor
words: When he touched my forehead, I felt like nobody owned me. Just for a minute.

speaker: debtor
words: I'd pay a copper for that again.

speaker: fen
words: Owe nobody.

speaker: fen
words: Owe nobody. No copper.

speaker: fen
words: It's a worse business. It's a better sermon.

speaker: fen
words: Bless you.

speaker: fen
words: See? It comes naturally.

speaker: fen
words: There. Just a hand.

speaker: fen
words: You'll find there are others. There's always others.

speaker: fen
words: The Unsworn's own blessing! Witnessed!

speaker: pip
words: You following me?

speaker: pip
words: Two crowns a run. Most I've ever earned. You're not spoiling it.

speaker: pip
words: And I don't open them. Open one and you don't get paid. Everyone knows that.

speaker: pip
words: Mr Pell. From the counting house. He's all right. Pays on time.

speaker: pip
words: You're on.

speaker: pip
words: Bet you didn't think I had one.

speaker: pip
words: Two crowns.

speaker: pip
words: Told you.

speaker: wren
words: The Bread of Dawn. That's the loaf they give out at dawn prayers.

speaker: pip
words: What's that mean?

speaker: pip
words: Thanks. Don't follow me again.

speaker: pip
words: That's two crowns! And Mr Pell'll know!

speaker: aldric
words: The Bread of Dawn feeds three thousand people a morning. His Grace would never put the Temple in that man's debt.

speaker: aldric
words: I'll ask him.

speaker: pip
words: What's the pay?

speaker: pip
words: ...Does Ser Aldric go past the stables?

speaker: corvin
words: Up early for a pilgrim. The Sundial's beautiful at dawn, isn't it? People come from all over.

speaker: corvin
words: Old Maren sent you, I expect. She's had a hard life. It would be such a shame to make it harder.

speaker: corvin
words: Good.

speaker: corvin
words: Two thousand years of pilgrims' feet. Stone wears.

speaker: corvin
words: Go and tell Maren that.

speaker: maren
words: He came, didn't he. Smiling.

speaker: maren
words: Well. You've got sense. More than I had.

speaker: maren
words: He came, didn't he. And you said it to his face.

speaker: maren
words: Wait there.

speaker: maren
words: The old readings. I copied them the week before they threw me out. Thirty years they've been in my bread tin.

speaker: maren
words: I'm too old to be brave on my own. Take them, and send for me when it's time.

speaker: captain
words: Ten lashes, for opening the Goddess's gate against the Hierarch's order. At noon.

speaker: hale
words: Don't.

speaker: hale
words: I opened it. Nobody made me. It's mine to pay.

speaker: captain
words: A sworn duel over a Sun Guard sentence?

speaker: captain
words: If you win, it's his rank and no lash. If you lose, he takes twenty. Still want it?

speaker: captain
words: Still want it?

speaker: hale
words: Suit yourself.

speaker: hale
words: You stood there.

speaker: hale
words: Most don't.

speaker: hale
words: You don't let a man pay his own way, do you.

speaker: hale
words: Thank you.

speaker: hale
words: Twenty, then.

speaker: hale
words: Stand where I can see you.
